fact: A Le Defi Media blog of 14 February 2026 says successive Mauritian political parties have promised Freedom of Information and failed to deliver, and that Senior Counsel Rama Valayden urges the government to introduce it; no law or bill is mentioned, and his 2022 draft is a constitutional amendment to section 12.
UNESCO's readiness assessment profile notes an absence of a Freedom of Information law in Mauritius.
Defimedia reports that the 2025-2029 Government Programme announced a Freedom of Information Act and that none of the transparency measures including it has been achieved so far.

Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam told parliament on 28 October 2025 that only exploratory drafting of a Freedom of Information Bill had begun at the Attorney General's office and an older bill was under review, and l'express says the bill has still not been presented to the National Assembly.
